newsitem.title: USA: Mass.'s Cellucci sees no new taxes or toll hikes.
newsitem.headline: Mass.'s Cellucci sees no new taxes or toll hikes.

text.p: Massachusetts Acting Governor Paul Cellucci told reporters he is committed to not raising taxes or tolls on the state's highways despite escalating costs of the "Big Dig" construction project in downtown Boston.
"Our commitment is that we see no need to raise tolls in the next five years and I see no need to raise taxes at all," he told reporters before a press conference on a cut in Internet sales taxes.
"In fact, I'm trying to cut taxes. I made a commitment I'm not going to raise taxes, and I haven't done it, and I will not," he said.

A U.S. General Accounting Office report now puts the price tag for the "Big Dig", the nation's most expensive transportation construction project, at $11.6 billion - $800 million more than state officials said.
In March, state officials estimated that the project, originally to cost $2.5 billion when it was proposed in 1985, would now cost $10.4 billion.
"What the GAO report indicates is that we now have to manage this huge project," Cellucci said.
He said that the state will stick with its $10.4 billion estimate, and try to trim costs elsewhere if other costs rise.
"If something goes up, something else will have to come down," he said.
